subtopic: Interconversion of States — Melting, Boiling, Sublimation
stem:
Observe the given figure carefully.

(The figure is a state-change diagram with three labelled boxes — "Ice", "Water" and "Water vapour". Arrows mark six processes: I is Ice → Water, IV is Water → Ice, II is Water → Water vapour, V is Water vapour → Water, III is Ice → Water vapour, and VI is Water vapour → Ice.)

Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Latent heat for process I is \(3.34 \times 10^{5}\) J/kg.

options.label: B
options.text: Processes I, II and III are endothermic while processes IV, V and VI are exothermic.

options.label: C
options.text: None of these

options.label: D
options.text: Water vapours formed during process II when come in contact with skin give out \(22.5 \times 10^{5}\) J/kg more heat than the boiling water.

stem:
An experiment is performed as shown in the given figure.

(The figure shows a beaker of water; on adding salt the salt first settles at the bottom of the beaker, and on stirring the salt particles spread uniformly throughout the water, occupying the spaces between the water particles.)

The conclusion we can draw from the given experiment is that
1. Nature of matter is continuous.
2. Matter is made up of particles.
3. Particles of salt get into the spaces between the particles of water.
4. Both Matter is made up of particles and particles of salt get into the spaces between the particles of water.

options.label: A
options.text: Statement (iv) is correct.

options.label: B
options.text: Statement (iii) is correct.

options.label: C
options.text: Statement (i) is correct.

options.label: D
options.text: Statement (ii) is correct.

subtopic: States of Matter and Their Properties
stem:
Diagrams W, X and Y show how the particles of a substance are packed at different temperatures.

(The figure shows three boxes: W has a few widely separated particles (gas); X has particles tightly and regularly packed (solid); Y has particles loosely and irregularly packed, closer than in W but with gaps unlike X (liquid). A second figure is a heating curve plotting Temperature (y-axis) against Time (x-axis) with four regions: I (temperature rising), II (flat plateau), III (temperature rising), IV (flat plateau then rising).)

The given graph shows the temperature changes which occur on warming the substance. In which region of the graph would all the particles be packed as in Y?

options.label: A
options.text: I

options.label: B
options.text: II

options.label: C
options.text: III

options.label: D
options.text: IV

subtopic: Interconversion of States — Melting, Boiling, Sublimation
stem:
Study the given heating curve of substance X carefully and select the correct statement.

(The figure plots Temperature (y-axis, with 273 and 373 marked) against Change of state (x-axis). Starting at P the curve rises through point 1 to Q at 273, runs flat from Q to R (point 2), rises through point 3 to S at 373, runs flat from S to T (point 4), then rises through point 5.)

options.label: A
options.text: Substance X exists in solid state at point 1, in liquid state at point 3 and in gaseous state at point 5.

options.label: B
options.text: At QR, matter exists both in solid and liquid states, while at ST matter exists both in liquid and gaseous states.

options.label: C
options.text: All of these

options.label: D
options.text: QR represents latent heat of fusion, while ST represents latent heat of vaporisation.

subtopic: Interconversion of States — Melting, Boiling, Sublimation
stem:
The correct set-up for finding the melting point of ice is:

(The figure shows four set-ups, each with a thermometer and a container of crushed ice. In set-up (a) the thermometer bulb hangs in the air above the crushed ice (not immersed). In set-up (b) the thermometer bulb is fully immersed inside the crushed ice in the container. In set-up (c) the thermometer bulb rests at the very bottom of the container touching only a thin layer of ice. In set-up (d) the thermometer is laid horizontally, separate from the container of crushed ice.)

options.label: A
options.text: Set-up (a) — thermometer bulb held in air above the crushed ice.

options.label: B
options.text: Set-up (b) — thermometer bulb fully immersed in the crushed ice.

options.label: C
options.text: Set-up (c) — thermometer bulb resting at the bottom of the container.

options.label: D
options.text: Set-up (d) — thermometer laid horizontally, outside the crushed ice.

subtopic: Interconversion of States — Melting, Boiling, Sublimation
stem:
Observe the given diagram showing changes in states of matter carefully.

(The figure shows three states arranged left to right: Gas — Liquid — Solid. Between Solid and Liquid: process P is Solid → Liquid and process S is Liquid → Solid. Between Liquid and Gas: process Q is Liquid → Gas and process R is Gas → Liquid. A top arrow U goes Gas → Solid, and a bottom arrow T goes Solid → Gas; the bottom path is labelled "Increase heat and decrease pressure".)

Which of the following is correct identification for processes P to U?

options.label: A
options.text: Q - Vaporisation, S - Liquefication, U - Solidification

options.label: B
options.text: P - Melting, Q - Condensation, S - Solidification

options.label: C
options.text: S - Sublimation, P - Liquefication, U - Solidification

options.label: D
options.text: P - Fusion, R - Condensation, T - Sublimation
